beats.text: 130 ships. One invasion. Then the wind.
beats.say: One hundred and thirty ships. One invasion. Then the wind.

beats.text: Queen Elizabeth of England was Philip's former sister-in-law. She had become his worst enemy.
Her captains, like Francis Drake, raided Spain's treasure fleets. And she sent troops to help the Dutch rebels.
Then she executed the Catholic Queen of Scots. Philip called for a crusade.
The Armada sailed from Lisbon. The plan: sweep up the Channel, collect an army in Flanders, and land in England.
At midnight off Calais, the English sent burning ships into the anchored fleet. The Armada scattered in panic.
The next day, at Gravelines, English guns tore into it.
Then came the wind. The fleet fled around Scotland and Ireland, and storms smashed dozens of ships on the rocks.
Thousands of men never came home.
Legend says Philip only sighed: I sent my ships against men, not against the wind.
He died ten years later in his small room at El Escorial. His empire was still vast. And bankrupt, for the fourth time.
